To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sustained, spatial activity patterns can exist in neuronal populations without recurrent excitation and that these patterns are pinned to specific spatial positions in the network when the coupling is inhomogeneous.
sustained spatial patterns of activity can arise in neuronal populations with no recurrent excitation.

sustained, spatial activity patterns in neuronal populations can be supported by a synaptic architecture without recurrent excitation; the bump that arises in this architecture is linearly stable, but at most one bump can exist for each background input value; this bump can be born, move, and die as background input changes; and spatial inhomogeneity can induce bump pinning.
